questions.note: Height, head size and shoulder line land close to the reference in the onion. What looks off is the volume: the upper arms are smooth, inflated tubes, the forearm guards and elbow pads add more girth than real armour would, and the man reads stockier and more robotic than the lean V-taper. Legs follow the declared real thigh lengths.

Stance, foot spread, elbow positions and the diagonal carbine line follow the reference well in the onion. The outline still looks CG: the elbows end in flat-faced cylinders, the pauldrons are rigid slabs standing off the shoulders, the trouser hems balloon into lumpy cuffs, and the hard-edged hair cap flattens the head's outline.

Every listed item is present and roughly where the drawing puts it: gaiter, carrier with three mag pouches, antenna, pauldrons, forearm guards, gloves, leg rigs, knee pads, boots. Some sizes are wrong: the gloves run as long tubes up the forearm into the guards, the knee pads are oversized bulbous shells, and the right thigh pouches are big hard boxes.

Nothing clearly passes through anything else, but several layers fail to rest on what is under them. The pauldrons hover on the shoulders. At the right elbow, forearm, guard and elbow pad telescope into each other like nested pipes. The trouser seat is shrink-wrapped to the buttocks, and the glove cuffs merge into the forearm guards with no visible wrist.

Bulk is in the wrong places. The sleeves are smooth and over-inflated while the shirt torso is flat black with no folds. The carrier front is a thin blank slab with none of the reference's stacked webbing bulk. The trousers are tight at the seat yet lumpy and noisy on the shins. Knee pads and thigh boxes read as moulded plastic, not padded cordura.

The carbine's angle and position across the body match the reference, and the right index finger lies straight along the receiver as a real trigger discipline would. The left hand reads loose, though: in the three-quarter view the palm opens away from the handguard instead of wrapping it. The stock rests against nothing, so the gun reads as placed between the hands, not held.

defects.what: The hair is a smooth dark shell with a hard, sharp rim at the forehead and temple and a few detached spiky fragments on the crown: it reads as a moulded toy wig.
defects.fix: Short hair thins into the skin at the hairline and temples, with individual strands and scalp showing through on the sides; the crown has a tousled, continuous volume.

defects.what: The skin is uniform, waxy and pinkish, with flat dark eye sockets, no stubble beyond a faint jaw shadow, and no pores or specular breakup: a mannequin face.
defects.fix: Weathered skin varies in redness and roughness, and has stubble over the jaw, chin and upper lip, wet eyes with lid margins, and a broken-up specular sheen.

defects.what: The top edges of both pauldrons are ragged and stair-stepped, like delaminated cardboard (also at x1475-1700, y600-830): a geometry artefact, not wear.
defects.fix: A moulded armour plate has a clean rolled or bevelled edge; wear shows as scuffed paint and chips on that edge, not as torn geometry.

defects.what: At the right elbow, the elbow pad is a flat-ended cylinder and the forearm guard and gloved forearm slide out of it like nested pipes, with no sleeve fabric bunching between them.
defects.fix: A real elbow pad is a domed cap strapped over the bent sleeve; the sleeve bunches in the crook, and the forearm guard sits separately on the forearm below.

defects.what: The right pauldron is a rigid flat slab hovering over the shoulder, with a dark gap beneath it and nothing pulling it onto the deltoid.
defects.fix: Shoulder armour is strapped or hung from the carrier's shoulder strap, so it follows the curve of the deltoid and touches the sleeve along its lower edge.

defects.what: The cloth-simulated lower trouser legs are covered in fine, even lumps like crumpled foil instead of a few large folds.
defects.fix: Heavy ripstop trousers form a few large, soft folds down the shin and stack into a handful of deep folds where they blouse over the boot.

defects.what: The trouser seat is shrink-wrapped to the buttocks, showing the cleft and the gluteal folds as on bare skin.
defects.fix: Combat trousers have a gusseted, loose seat that bridges across the cleft and hangs in a soft drape below the buttocks.

defects.what: The right boot's foot is a seamless, rubbery shell like a galosh: no toe cap, no panel seams, no stitching and no creasing at the flex point.
defects.fix: A Zephyr-class boot shows a stitched suede and textile upper, a rubber toe bumper, panel seams and a crease across the vamp where the foot flexes.

defects.what: The knee pads are bulbous, uniformly glossy shells whose wear is a flat painted band along the bottom edge: they read as toy plastic.
defects.fix: AirFlex-class caps are faceted, matte, hard caps with moulded ribs, scuffed and scratched all over, held by visible elastic straps.

defects.what: The right thigh magazine pouches are smooth grey hard-plastic boxes with stamped slots, unlike the worn fabric pouches beside them.
defects.fix: A drop-leg mag pouch is cordura with bound edges, stitching, elastic retention and a dirty, matte weave.

defects.what: The carbine is uniformly matte grey with a few tan stripes: no anodised-versus-polymer contrast, no edge wear and no dirt, so it reads as a clean toy.
defects.fix: A used M4 contrasts anodised aluminium (receiver, handguard) with polymer (stock, grip, magazine), and its edges, controls and contact points are worn bright.

defects.what: The handguard's top rail renders as a high-contrast black-and-white zebra hatch that reads like a texture or moire, not machined slots.
defects.fix: Rail slots read as dark recesses between dull anodised ribs, with soft shading and a low-contrast edge highlight.

defects.what: The left forearm guard is a cone that the arm disappears into, and the glove runs as a smooth tube up to it with no wrist, closure or cuff detail.
defects.fix: A Mechanix-class glove ends at the wrist with a velcro closure tab; the sleeve cuff shows between it and the separately strapped forearm guard.

defects.what: The left hand's palm opens away from the handguard instead of wrapping it, so the support hand does not visibly close on the gun.
defects.fix: The support hand wraps the handguard, thumb over the top or along the side, fingers curled under and pressing in.

defects.what: The carrier front is a blank, thin slab with crisp edges: no PALS rows, no admin pouch, no webbing loops and no fabric softness at the edges.
defects.fix: A JPC-class front flap carries PALS webbing or a loop panel, its edges are bound and slightly rounded, and the fabric puckers where straps pull.

defects.what: The trouser camo has a perfectly regular square grid printed over soft blotches, too even and too visible for ripstop at this distance.
defects.fix: The ripstop grid is barely visible at this distance; the fabric shows instead as uneven fading, dirt at the knees and hems, and dust in the folds.

defects.what: The boots have only a faint soft shadow under them, with no dark contact line, so the feet look set onto the floor rather than standing on it.
defects.fix: A boot on concrete shows a thin, dark occlusion line where the sole meets the floor, under a softer cast shadow.

ranked: [D2] The face is a waxy, pink, uniform mannequin: dark empty sockets, no stubble, no skin breakup. At native size it gives the whole figure away as CG before anything else.
[D1] The hair is a hard-edged dark cap with stray spikes on top, a toy-figure wig rather than short tousled hair thinning out at the temples.

Materials overall are flat and clean: grey plastic plates, flat black shirt, matte grey gun. The reference is olive and tan, worn and dirty everywhere; the render reads as an untextured game-asset blockout.
[D4] The right elbow is a stack of nested cylinders, elbow pad, guard and forearm telescoping like pipes, which reads as robot armour, not kit strapped over cloth.
[D13] The left forearm guard is a cone swallowing the arm, and the glove continues as a smooth tube up to it: there is no wrist, closure or sleeve cuff.
[D5] [D3] The pauldrons are rigid slabs hovering over the shoulders, and their top edges break into ragged stair-stepped geometry in the closer views.
The upper sleeves are smooth, inflated tubes with no folds at the armpit or under the armband, yet the forearms are skin-tight: the cloth looks over-pressurised rather than draped.
[D6] The cloth-simulated shins are covered in fine, even lumps like crumpled foil; real trousers fold in a few large planes and stack deeply over the boot.
[D7] The trouser seat is shrink-wrapped to the buttocks, showing the cleft; combat trousers bridge and hang there.
[D9] The knee pads are bulbous glossy shells with a painted wear band, reading as toy plastic rather than matte, faceted, scratched caps.
[D8] The right boot's foot is a seamless galosh: no toe bumper, no panel seams, no flex creases. The two boots also differ in value and wear, so they look made by two different methods.
[D10] The right thigh mag pouches are hard grey plastic boxes with stamped slots, unlike the worn olive fabric pouches on the other leg.
[D11] The carbine is one matte grey with tan stripes, with no anodised-versus-polymer contrast and no edge wear; it reads as a clean prop.
[D14] The left hand does not close on the handguard: from three-quarter left the palm opens away from it, so the hold reads as posed.
[D15] The carrier front is a blank thin slab with crisp corners; the reference's carrier has bulk from webbing, admin pouch and straps.
The shirt is flat black with almost no folds across the torso, flanks or elbow crooks, so it reads as a painted body rather than fabric.
The thighs read almost solid black while the lower legs carry strong camo blotches: the trouser texture changes between upper and lower leg.
[D16] The ripstop grid is printed too regularly and too visibly over the camo.
[D12] The handguard rail is a black-and-white zebra hatch that reads as moire, not machined slots.
[D17] Contact shadows under the boots are faint, so the figure looks set onto the floor rather than standing on it.
